strings.step.1.description: Install the tools needed to read, inspect and modify your BIOS. Download any missing tools below; the app checks each file for you.
strings.step.2.description: Open a BIOS file you already have, or save a copy of the BIOS installed on this computer. The original file is kept unchanged.
strings.step.3.description: See what is already installed in your BIOS and which changes are available. Review the results, then continue to choose your modifications.
strings.step.4.description: Use the recommendations for this computer's CPU, or choose Custom settings when you want different changes or are preparing a BIOS for another system.
strings.step.5.description: Create a new BIOS file with your selected changes. The app checks the result before making it available to save or flash.
strings.step.6.description: Save the verified BIOS file for later, or flash it to this computer. Flashing first creates and checks two independent backups of the installed BIOS.

strings.fpt.confirm:
Flash this verified BIOS to the computer running SenorX99?

{path}

Make sure this BIOS is intended for this motherboard and the CPU that will be used with it. The app creates two independent backups and requires them to match before writing. If writing fails after erasing or programming begins, it attempts to restore the verified backup.

Do not restart, remove power or close the app during flashing or recovery. An interrupted write can leave the motherboard unable to start and require an external programmer.

Proceed with flashing?

strings.config.tbu_warning:
Turbo Boost Unlock is intended for supported Xeon E5-26xx v3 CPUs.

Using this hack with an E5 v4 CPU may prevent POST: the computer may be unable to complete its startup checks or boot into Windows.

The CPU in this computer does not restrict your choices; you may be preparing this BIOS for another system. Continue only if the target system will use a compatible E5-26xx v3 CPU.

Include Turbo Boost Unlock?

strings.help.title: What does this modification do?
strings.help.prompt: Click a question mark beside a modification to read its explanation here.
strings.help.tbu:
Turbo Boost Unlock aims to keep all CPU cores running at the processor's maximum turbo frequency under load, instead of reducing the turbo ratio as more cores become active. This can substantially improve performance in work that uses many cores.

SenorX99 removes the relevant 06F2 microcode, adjusts the required CPU power-state defaults and installs the selected ser8989 S3TurboHack firmware component. The result is checked as one complete modification.

−60/−50/−50 mV is the recommended starting profile: Core / Cache / System Agent. Lower voltage can reduce power consumption and heat, giving the CPU more headroom to sustain higher all-core turbo clocks. Individual CPUs differ, so a profile still needs stability testing on the target system.

The aim is sustained maximum all-core turbo under load. Actual clocks still depend on workload, cooling and power/current limits. The hack does not turn a v4 CPU into a compatible v3 CPU. Choose this option only for a supported E5-26xx v3 target system.
strings.help.secureboot:
Secure Boot uses certificates to decide which startup software is trusted. This option updates outdated factory certificates stored inside the BIOS to the included validated 2023-capable set, and replaces an AMI test Platform Key when required. The revoked-signature database (dbx) is preserved.

Certificates stored in a BIOS file are different from the keys currently enrolled on a running motherboard. After flashing, your BIOS may require restoring its factory Secure Boot keys before the new defaults become enrolled. If this ROM is already up to date, an update is not recommended.
strings.help.overclock:
This exposes the supported BIOS overclocking controls and applies the related defaults. It does not automatically overclock the CPU or choose a clock speed.

Recommended CPUs are Xeon E5-1650 v3, E5-1660 v3, E5-1680 v3 and Core i7-5820K, 5930K, 5960X, 6800K, 6850K, 6900K and 6950X. The BIOS must also contain the supported setup structures.

The modification disables Overclocking Lock, enables the current override and exposes the ratio/current-control menus. You configure the actual overclock in BIOS afterwards and test its stability. CPU detection only guides recommendations; Custom settings can prepare a ROM for a different system.
strings.help.splash:
This changes the picture displayed when the computer starts. Recommended mode uses the included image, matched to the BIOS image format. In Custom settings you can choose your own BMP.

Before offering a custom image, the app performs a real replacement on a temporary BIOS copy and checks the extracted image and firmware integrity. If this check fails, the option shows N/A. The final built ROM is checked again. Uncheck the modification in Custom settings to keep the existing logo.
strings.help.optimized_intro:
These are performance-oriented default BIOS settings. They remain the values restored when you load BIOS defaults. Settings already at their target values are kept.

The exact changes for this ROM are:
strings.help.optimized_end: Disabling power-saving options may increase idle power use. Disabling memory scrubbing removes those particular ECC maintenance features; the ECC operating mode itself is not changed.
strings.reason.ACPI T-States: Avoids CPU throttling through ACPI T-states to favour performance.
strings.reason.SATA AHCI ALPM: Avoids aggressive power-saving transitions and wake-up delays on the main SATA controller.
strings.reason.sSATA AHCI ALPM: Avoids aggressive power-saving transitions on the secondary SATA controller.
strings.reason.Patrol Scrub: Stops background ECC-memory scans and corrective write-backs, reducing maintenance work while removing that protection.
strings.reason.Demand Scrub: Stops corrective write-back after a correctable ECC read error, reducing scrubbing work while removing that maintenance protection.
strings.reason.Memory Power Savings Mode: Avoids memory power-saving entry and wake-up transitions.
strings.reason.MDLL Off: Keeps the memory delay-locked loop from shutting down during self-refresh.
strings.reason.Energy Performance Tuning: Uses the BIOS performance-bias setting instead of delegating that tuning choice to the operating system.
strings.reason.SATA AHCI LPM: Avoids link power-saving transitions on the main SATA controller.
strings.reason.sSATA AHCI LPM: Avoids link power-saving transitions on the secondary SATA controller.
